items.actClause:
AN ACT to amend the public authorities law, in relation to requiring service
providers to annually submit emergency response plans to the public service
commission
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S968

SPONSOR: GAUGHRAN
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the public authorities law, in relation to requiring
service providers to annually submit emergency response plans to the
public service commission

 
PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL:

The purpose of this legislation is to outline criteria to be included in
the Long Island Power Authority and its service provider's emergency
response plans, and subject them to review, approval and enforcement by
the Public Service Commission.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1: Amends subdivision (cc) of section 1020-f of the public
authorities law to require the authority to submit its service providers
emergency response plan to the public service commission for review and
approval on or before December 15 annually; set requirements for what
the plan shall include; grant the commission authority to amend the plan
and investigate the performance the service providers in restoring
service or meeting the requirements laid out in their plan; require that
the plan be filed with relevant parties within service territory and
that it be available pursuant to article six of public officers law.

Section 2: Amends subdivision 1 of section 1020-s of the public authori-
ties law to allow commission review, approval and enforcement of emer-
gency management plans by LIPA and its service provider, including the
ability to assess penalties and remedies for violations.

Section 3: Sets the effective date.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

The LIPA Reform Act of 2013 restructured Long Island's electric oper-
ations, and shifted oversight of management and operations to the Long
Island Power Authority. In doing so, the Public Service Commission,
which oversees all other utilities in the New York State, does not regu-
late or have oversight of electric utility operations on Long Island and
the Rockaway Peninsula. LIPA contracts with a service provider, current-
ly PSEG Long Island, to operate its electric system.

On August 4, 2020, Tropical Storm Isaias revealed significant vulner-
abilities in the preparedness of LIPA and its service provider to quick-
ly restore power to more than 420,000 impacted customers. Multiple days
later, tens of thousands were still without power. The storm revealed
widespread communications failures during and in the aftermath of the
storm, leaving customers in the dark without vital information to make
decisions regarding their health and safety. This was especially danger-
ous for medically vulnerable customers, including those on oxygen and
those that are part of the service provider's "Critical Care Program,"
many of whom LIPA and its service provider failed to prioritize.

Electric utilities across New York State are required to develop, main-
tain and adhere to emergency response plans as reviewed and approved by
the Public Service Commission. However, unlike every other electric
utility in New York State, LIPA's service provider is not subject to
penalties or fines for its adherence to its emergency response plan
because it is not regulated by, or have its plan reviewed and approved,
by the entire Public Service Commission. This legislation is necessary
to correct this. LIPA's service provider should be held accountable for
its failure to successfully implement its emergency response plan and
reasonably restore services during an emergency event.

 
PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

2020: S8913/A10947

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

None.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
The act shall take effect immediately.

title: Relates to requiring service providers to prepare and submit emergency response plans

items.memoText:
VETO MESSAGE - No. 92
 
TO THE SENATE:
 
I am returning herewith, without my approval, the following bill:
 
Senate Bill Number 968-A, entitled:
 
    "AN  ACT to amend the public authorities law, in relation to requir-
      ing service providers to annually submit emergency response  plans
      to the public service commission"
 
    NOT APPROVED
 
  This  bill  would  require  the  Long Island Power Authority (LIPA) to
submit its service provider's  emergency  response  plan  (ERP)  to  the
Public Service Commission for annual review and approval.
 
  Currently,  pursuant  to the LIPA Reform Act, the Department of Public
Service (DPS) reviews, and the LIPA Board approves, the service  provid-
er's ERP. In addition, the contract between LIPA and its service provid-
er  was  renegotiated  in 2021 to contain stronger provisions for review
and approval of the service provider's ERP by DPS and the LIPA Board  of
Trustees.  In  addition,  the  newly-created  New York State Legislative
Commission on the Future of the Long  Island  Power  Authority  will  be
providing  a  final report by April 1, 2023 that covers topics including
improved storm response.
 
  Ensuring Long Islanders have safe, reliable power  sources  throughout
the  year,  especially  during emergencies, is a worthy goal. Because of
the significant ongoing work related to the subject of this bill,  I  am
constrained to veto this bill.
 
  The bill is disapproved.                       (signed) KATHY HOCHUL
 
                               __________
